grid.levelButton: {level} — click to change the name, level or unit of {name}
grid.emptyHelp: Type the variable names in the first row and the data below them. Or copy a table from Excel or Google Sheets (names in the first row), click the first cell and press Ctrl+V.
grid.emptyExamples: No data at hand? Open Example data.
grid.fingerprintHelp: A code computed from the pasted values. The same data always gives the same code, so an assistant who pastes your sheet can check that your report came from it. Renaming variables does not change it.
warn.headerNumeric: The first row looks like numbers, but it was used as the variable names. If your table has no row of names, add one in Excel and paste again.
warn.coded: {name}: is this a coded category (1 = Male, 2 = Female)? Change it to nominal in the variable dialog.
warn.id: Looks like an ID column; it cannot be used as a grouping variable.
warn.codedShort: Is this a coded category? Click the type label in the grid to change it to nominal.
warn.nonNumeric: {name}: {count} cells are not numbers and count as missing.
paste.empty: The clipboard holds no table. Copy cells from Excel or Google Sheets first.
paste.noRows: Only one row was pasted. The first row must hold the variable names and the rows below it the data.
confirm.replaceBody: The data in the grid will be replaced by the new table.
confirm.newBody: The data in the grid will be removed.
confirm.reportCleared: Everything in the report will also be cleared. Download or print it first if you need it.
variable.title: Variable
variable.name: Name
variable.ratioHelp: Needed for the coefficient of variation (CV).
variable.nameTaken: Another variable already has this name.
settings.title: Settings
settings.invalidHelp: Cells holding one of these codes count as missing, as do empty cells. One code per line. This list resets when the page is reloaded.
settings.decimalHelp: Auto reads each column the way it is written, and shows results with a comma in Bahasa Indonesia and a point in English. Comma or Point applies to both reading and showing.
tabs.label: Analyses
picker.noData: Paste data above to choose variables.
section.comingSoon: The results for this tab are still being built.
report.title: Report
report.clearConfirm: Remove every item from the report?
report.empty: Nothing here yet. Use Add to report under any table or chart.
report.notSaved: Not saved — download or print before closing this page.
grid.label: Data table
grid.help: Click a cell and type, or paste a block with Ctrl+V. Right-click to insert or delete rows and columns; Ctrl+Z undoes.
grid.notSaved: Nothing is saved: use Copy data to keep your edits in Excel or Google Sheets.
notice.dataCopied: The whole table is on the clipboard. Paste it into Excel or Google Sheets to keep it.
notice.copyFailed: The browser did not allow copying. Select the cells and press Ctrl+C instead.
confirm.editsLost: Your edits are not saved anywhere. Use Copy data first if you want to keep them.
variable.valuesHint: To change values, edit the cells in the grid. Changing the name, level or unit never changes the data.
report.staleNote: Made from an earlier version of the data (fingerprint {fingerprint}); the data was edited afterwards.
describe.heading: Descriptive statistics
describe.pick: Tick one or more variables above to describe them.
describe.cvNote: CV is shown only for a variable on a ratio scale (tick "Ratio scale" in the variable dialog) with a positive mean.
describe.quartileNote: Q1 and Q3 (QUARTILE.EXC) need at least 3 values.
describe.groupId: {name} looks like an ID column, so it cannot be used to form groups. Untick it or change it in the variable dialog.
describe.firstGroupOnly: Only the first ticked nominal or ordinal variable ({name}) is used to form groups.
describe.twoOnly: Only the first two ticked nominal or ordinal variables are cross-tabulated.
describe.interp.summary: {name}: {n} values were used{missing}. The mean is {mean}{unit} and the standard deviation is {sd}{unit}, so a typical value lies about {sd}{unit} away from the mean. The values run from {min} to {max}{unit}.
describe.interp.quartiles: Half of the values are at or below the median of {median}{unit}; the middle half lies between Q1 = {q1} and Q3 = {q3}.
describe.interp.skewRight: The skewness of {skew} is positive: the distribution has a longer tail towards high values.
describe.interp.skewLeft: The skewness of {skew} is negative: the distribution has a longer tail towards low values.
describe.interp.skewNone: The skewness of {skew} is close to zero: the distribution is roughly symmetric.
describe.interp.cv: The coefficient of variation is {cv}%: the standard deviation is {cv}% of the mean.
describe.interp.ci: The {level}% confidence interval for the mean runs from {lower} to {upper}{unit}. An interval built this way contains the population mean in {level}% of samples.
describe.ciUnreliable: † n·p̂ or n·(1 − p̂) is below 5 for this category, so its interval is unreliable; more data is needed.
describe.interp.freq: The table counts how often each category of {name} occurs among {n} valid values{missing}. The most frequent category is {top} ({count} values, {pct}%). The cumulative % adds up the shares from the top row down.
describe.interp.freqCi: For each category, the {level}% confidence interval (Wald) estimates the share of that category in the population.
describe.interp.cont: The counts table shows how many cases fall in each combination of {row} and {col}, out of {n} cases with both values{missing}. Row % shows how {col} is spread within each category of {row}; column % shows how {row} is spread within each category of {col}.
describe.noOutliers: No values lie outside the fences.
describe.outlierAdvice: Investigate these values; do not delete them automatically. If they change the conclusion, report the results with and without them.
chart.swNA: Shapiro–Wilk needs 3 to 5000 values that are not all equal.
chart.swCaption: A p-value above 0.05 does not prove normality. Judge from the histogram and the Q-Q plot; with n ≥ 30 per group the methods here are robust.
ss.heading: Sample size
ss.sigmaHelp: From an earlier study, or paste 10–15 pilot values below to compute it.
ss.pHelp: Use 50% if you have no estimate; it gives the largest n.
ss.invalid: Enter a positive value for every input (p between 0 and 100%).
ss.interp.mean: With {level}% confidence, a standard deviation of {sigma}{unit} and a margin of error of ±{e}{unit}, each group needs at least {n} cases (always rounded up). With {groups} group(s), plan for {total} cases in total.
ss.interp.prop: With {level}% confidence, an expected proportion of {p}% and a margin of error of ±{e} percentage points, each group needs at least {n} cases (always rounded up). With {groups} group(s), plan for {total} cases in total.
ss.minMean: At least 30 per group when comparing means.
ss.minProp: For proportions, n·p ≥ 5 and n·(1 − p) ≥ 5 in every group.
ss.minChi: For a chi-square test, an expected count of at least 5 in every cell.
ss.belowMean: This is below 30 per group: plan for at least 30.
ss.belowProp: n·p or n·(1 − p) would be below 5: plan for a larger sample.
